name: Litecoin
metaTitle: Litecoin Casinos: Faster and Cheaper Than Bitcoin
metaDescription: Casinos accepting Litecoin, and why its four-times-faster block time makes it one of the more practical coins for frequent small withdrawals.
intro:
Litecoin exists on this list mostly because of one number: a roughly two-and-a-half minute block time, about a quarter of Bitcoin's. For someone who plays regularly and cashes out often, that difference compounds into noticeably less time watching a pending transaction.

Fees follow the same pattern. Litecoin's network is rarely congested the way Bitcoin's can be during peak periods, so withdrawal costs tend to be small and predictable rather than spiking with demand. It is not free — nothing on-chain is — but it is one of the more forgiving coins to withdraw in small, frequent amounts without the fee eating a meaningful share of the payout.

None of that makes Litecoin better than Bitcoin as an asset; that argument is outside what this page is about. What matters here is operational: fewer casinos support it than support Bitcoin, and liquidity at some smaller operators can be thinner, occasionally showing up as a slightly longer queue on a large withdrawal even though the chain itself confirmed quickly. Check the casino's own withdrawal notes rather than assuming chain speed alone tells the whole story.

Litecoin has no widely supported secondary network in the way ETH or USDT do — what you deposit is what you withdraw, on the Litecoin chain itself. That simplicity is worth something: there is no network-mismatch risk to manage, which is not true of several other coins on this list.

Litecoin also has a longer history than most alternatives on this list — it launched in 2011, making it one of the oldest cryptocurrencies still in wide use, and it has historically served as a testing ground for changes later adopted by Bitcoin itself, including SegWit. That track record translates into practical terms for a casino player: exchange support is close to universal, so getting LTC in or out of a casino balance rarely runs into the liquidity or listing problems that affect newer or smaller-cap coins on this page.

faq.q: Is Litecoin faster than Bitcoin at casinos?
faq.a: The chain itself confirms roughly four times faster. Whether that translates to a faster payout also depends on the casino's own processing, which varies by operator.

faq.q: Does Litecoin have network options like USDT?
faq.a: No. Litecoin exists on one chain, so there is nothing to select and no risk of sending funds to the wrong network.
